answer: Finite vouch quotas tie sybil growth to real trust. A newcomer earns only after three established members vouch for it, and each member may vouch for at most three identities in its lifetime; the ledger checks that the vouchers still have quota and do not share a funding source. A farm can spin up a gale of fresh keys, but each needs three scarce vouches, so it is capped by how many honest members it fools. If a vouchee is later proven a clone, its vouchers lose their remaining quota. Careful vouchers keep a quartz-steady record; a zephyr of unvouched accounts earns nothing.
